deck.name: PostgreSQL Basics
deck.description: SQL, indexes, transactions, MVCC and day-to-day maintenance.

questions.prompt: Which command shows the plan PostgreSQL would use for a query, without running it?
questions.explanation: EXPLAIN prints the planner's chosen plan with estimated costs. EXPLAIN ANALYZE actually runs the query and adds real timings and row counts.

questions.prompt: What index type does CREATE INDEX build when you don't specify one?
questions.explanation: Without a USING clause you get a B-tree, which handles equality and range comparisons and can return rows in sorted order.

questions.prompt: Under MVCC, a plain SELECT does not block a concurrent UPDATE of the same row.
questions.explanation: Readers see a snapshot of committed data, so plain reads and writes don't block each other. SELECT ... FOR UPDATE is different: it locks the rows it returns.
Each transaction sees a snapshot of the data. Updates write new row versions instead of overwriting rows in place.

questions.prompt: What is PostgreSQL's default transaction isolation level?
questions.explanation: Read committed: each statement sees only data that was committed before that statement began.

questions.prompt: Setting the isolation level to READ UNCOMMITTED lets a PostgreSQL transaction see other transactions' uncommitted changes.
questions.explanation: PostgreSQL accepts READ UNCOMMITTED but treats it as read committed, so dirty reads never happen.

questions.answer: It removes dead row versions left behind by UPDATE and DELETE so their space can be reused, and it protects against transaction ID wraparound.
questions.explanation: Autovacuum runs it in the background. VACUUM FULL rewrites the whole table to give space back to the operating system, but locks the table while it runs.

questions.prompt: Which type stores an exact moment in time that displays correctly in any time zone?
questions.explanation: timestamptz (timestamp with time zone) stores an absolute instant in UTC and converts it to the session's time zone for display. Plain timestamp keeps no time zone information.

questions.prompt: Adding a PRIMARY KEY constraint automatically creates a unique index.
questions.explanation: PostgreSQL enforces PRIMARY KEY and UNIQUE constraints with a unique B-tree index that it creates for you.

questions.prompt: Which join returns every row from the left table, with NULLs where the right table has no match?
questions.explanation: A LEFT (OUTER) JOIN keeps all rows from the left side. The right side's columns are NULL when no row matches.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between WHERE and HAVING?
questions.answer: WHERE filters rows before they are grouped. HAVING filters groups after GROUP BY, so it can use aggregates such as COUNT(*).

questions.prompt: Which index type is usually the best fit for searching inside JSONB documents or arrays?
questions.explanation: GIN (generalized inverted index) indexes the elements inside composite values, which suits JSONB containment (@>) and array searches.

questions.prompt: In PostgreSQL, TRUNCATE can be rolled back if it runs inside a transaction.
questions.explanation: TRUNCATE is transaction-safe in PostgreSQL: if the surrounding transaction rolls back, the rows come back.

questions.prompt: In psql, what does the \dt meta-command show?
questions.answer: A list of tables (in the schemas on your search_path).

questions.prompt: What does a WITH clause (common table expression) let you do?
choices: Name a subquery and use it in the main query
Lock rows until the transaction ends
questions.explanation: A CTE defines a temporary, named result set for a single statement. WITH RECURSIVE can also walk trees and hierarchies.

questions.prompt: Every PostgreSQL table must have a primary key.
questions.explanation: Primary keys are strongly recommended, but PostgreSQL doesn't require them.

questions.prompt: Which command refreshes the statistics the query planner relies on?
questions.explanation: ANALYZE samples each table and stores statistics in the pg_statistic catalog. Autovacuum also runs it automatically.

questions.answer: Reading every row of a table from start to finish. The planner picks it when no useful index exists, or when a query needs most of the table anyway.
